card.name: Chronic or mouse before disease terms
card.fires_on: The words chronic, malignant and mouse when they come right before a disease or tumor term such as liver disease, mammary tumors or lymphoma. Seen in label text on thrombosis risk and genotoxicity tests.

modes.label: Chronic liver disease
modes.description: The word chronic placed before liver disease or hepatitis in patient-population statements.
modes.example: TPO receptor agonists have been associated with thrombotic and thromboembolic complications in patients with<< chronic>> liver disease.

modes.label: Mouse lymphoma assay
modes.description: The word mouse (or the start of lymphoma) in the name of a genotoxicity test.
modes.example: agenic potential of metformin alone in the following in vitro tests: Ames test (S. typhimurium), gene mutation test (<<mouse>> lymphoma cells), or chromosomal aberr

modes.label: Malignant tumors
modes.description: The word malignant before tumor terms in animal carcinogenicity findings.
modes.example: there was a statistically significant and dose-related increase in the incidence of<< malignant>> mammary tumors in female mice at fl

card.writes: It lowers the chance of the next word being acute or chronic, which fits a disease word already given.
card.plain: It marks a qualifier like chronic or mouse that has just been written before a disease or test name.
